chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, and Amr ibn Ibrahim, all from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:

A scorpion stung the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so he shook it off and said: 'May Allah curse you, for neither a believer nor an infidel is safe from you.' Then he called for salt, placed it upon the site of the sting, and pressed it with his thumb until it melted. Then he said: 'If people knew what is in the salt, they would not be in need of an antidote alongside it.'

key_terms.دِرْيَاق: Antidote or remedy (often referring to specific medicinal powders or substances)
key_terms.لَدْغَة: Sting or bite (specifically from a scorpion or snake)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of salt in the Prophet's treatment of a scorpion sting according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) demonstrates the prophetic use of salt as a therapeutic agent for scorpion stings, emphasizing its efficacy through physical application and verbal blessing. This incident underscores the Shia scholarly view of salt not merely as a condiment but as a divinely endowed remedy, reinforcing the concept of *tibb al-nabawi* (Prophetic medicine) where simple natural substances hold profound healing properties.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, and Amro Bin Ibrahim, altogether from Khalaf Bin Hammad, from yaqoub Bin Shuayb, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘A scorpion stung Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, so he<sup>saww</sup> shook it off and said: ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Curse you, for neither a Believer nor an Infidel is safe from you’. Then he<sup>saww</sup> called for the salt, so he<sup>saww</sup> placed it upon the place of the bite and pressed it by his<sup>saww</sup> thumb until it melted. Then he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘If the people knew what was in the salt, they would not be needy along with it, for any (other) antidote’.
en.sarwar: 10. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from his father and ‘Amr ibn Ibrahim all from Khalaf ibn Hammad from Ya’qub ibn Shu’ayb who has said the following: “Once, scorpion bit the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause. He (the Messenger of Allah) then threw it away, saying, ‘May Allah condemn you, both believers and unbelievers are not safe from you.’

He (the Messenger of Allah) then asked for salt, placed it on the bitten place and squeezed it with his thumb until it melted and then said, ‘Had people known that which is in salt, they would not need to seek any other antidote.’”
